hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -2}h(x)$ represents the limit of $h$ as $x$ approaches $-2$.

Although the function isn't defined at $x=-2$, the $y$-values seem to approach a distinct value as the $x$-values approach $-2$.

![The graph of function h has arrows pointing along the curve, down to the right and down to the left, respectively, pointing to the open circle.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/ded34fe68e274e0eeac995be43b33e39e84e9679)

The limit seems to be somewhere between $y=-7$ and $y=-6$, but slightly closer to $y=-6$.

![The graph of function h has a dashed horizontal line passing through the open circle, between y = negative 6 and y = negative 7, closer to y = negative 6.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/c3aede7b5d3efdef29cf75b19ed9c14df80278c5)

question.content:
The function $h$ is defined for all real numbers except for $x=-2$.

![Function h is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve. The curve starts in quadrant 2 and moves downward to an open circle at x = negative 2, just below y = negative 6. The curve moves upward to quadrant 1, moves downward, and end in quadrant 4.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/c4fdeae3d9507a9aff64e1d8d8ebf56e6c4dbf2c)

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -2}h(x)$ ?**
